To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the small cells and large cells of primary nodular lymphoma of the lung contain the same monoclonal immunobulin as the mature plasma cells observed in the interfollicu lar areas, that the DRCs observed within the tumor are supporting evidence of B cell derivation, and that a modification of the peroxidase antiperoxidase technique can demonstrate intracytoplasmie immunoglobulin more sensitively and specifically than the standard technique.

the peroxidase ‐antiperoxidate technique, when modified as described, is a highly sensitive and specific method for the identification of monoclonal Ig within the cytoplams of both the large and small cells of nodular pulmonary lymphoma.

the PAP method, using dilute antisera, prolonged incubation, and a modified substrate solution, is highly sensitive and specific in the identification of intracytoplasmatic immunoglobulins within the cytoplamic of both large cells and small cell of nodular lymphoma of the lung.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a rare form of lung cancer, primary nodular (nodular‐sclerosing) lymphoma.
the identification of primary nodular lymphoma of the lung by the application of histological, immunohistochemical, and ultrastructural techniques.
the use of the PAP and electron microscopic techniques in the study of two cases of primary nodular lymphoma of the lung.

both of the nodular lymphomas studied were of B cell origin, with the small cells and large cells being the neoplastic elements.
both of the lymphomas were primary nodular lymphoma of B cell derivation.

a diagnosis of a nodular lymphoma can be made on the basis of a single biopsy.
the PAP technique is a useful adjunct in the diagnosis of nodular lymphoma of the lung and that the DRC is a marker of the B cell origin of this lymphoma.
